hed: Iran’s Hormuz exclusion-zone plans remain as Brent clears $100 on wider Gulf fighting
dek: CENTCOM spokesperson Capt. Tim Hawkins’s Monday denial that Iran struck an uncrewed U.S. military vessel in the Strait of Hormuz — calling the claim a “total lie” — still stood Wednesday morning. Iran’s Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei has said Tehran would announce a restricted/exclusion zone and Hormuz shipping corridor maps, with an Oman corridor still discussed. Overnight U.S. destruction of five Iranian oil tankers and Iran’s claimed Jordan-base fire shifted the energy story to Brent about $100.07 and WTI near $94.73; this item tracks the standing Hormuz-zone and denial context separate from the tanker lead.
alt: A U.S. sailor stands watch on a warship as another vessel crosses the water
byline: Event summary from public reporting and named outlets

cl.body: AP denial coverage, Al-Monitor restricted-zone reporting, and Reuters oil desks pair CENTCOM’s standing denial with Rezaei’s corridor maps as Brent cleared $100 on wider fighting.

cr.body: Energy desks emphasize CENTCOM’s standing denial, throughput remarks, and oil above $100 as exclusion-zone and Oman corridor plans remain in play beside the tanker strikes.

seo_description: CENTCOM’s denial of an Iranian uncrewed-vessel strike claim still stands; Rezaei’s Hormuz corridor maps remain pending as Brent tops $100 after tanker strikes.
